item.title: Joe Mazzulla names one schematic blunder Celtics must fix, it's not about Jayson Tatum
item.description: Joe Mazzulla names one schematic blunder Celtics must fix, it's not about Jayson Tatum originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Boston Celtics thought they were peachy early in their 2026-27 NBA season. Then, they got slapped with a rough 109-93 loss to the Houston Rockets . Much of their identity on both ends of the floor collapsed. Everyone on Coach Joe Mazzulla's squad scored under 20 points, including Jayson Tatum. The Celtics' head coach admitted they made a schematic blunder after seeing the collapse. It all comes down to how they use Mitchell Robinson. Mazzulla names Celtics' schematic blunder that revolves around Robinson The Celtics were all but ready to face the league-leading Rockets. They were on a five-game winning streak entering this game, then everything fell apart. Jayson Tatum willed Coach Joe Mazzulla's squad to a first-quarter 29-point tie. Afterward, the Celtics just lagged in every aspect of the game. The Celtics did win the rebounding battle, with 38 total boards to the Rockets' 36. However, Coach Mazzulla noted this was the one aspect the Celtics needed to improve. It wasn't that Jayson Tatum and Co. all scored under 20 points; the focus is on fixing their rebounding woes. He further explained the problem on the boards by emphasizing that the Celtics weren't using Mitchell Robinson properly, via Jay King of The Athletic. "I would say for his (Mitchell Robinson) offensive rebounding impact, we have him a little bit further away from the rim, setting screens and playmaking for us on the perimeter as part of our offense. I think that has a little bit to do with it," the Celtics head coach declared. Robinson is averaging only 1.8 offensive rebounds and 4.5 boards in total. That's far from his previous season's average of 8.8 total rebounds and 4.2 offensive rebounds. His ORB% also dropped from a career-high 23.9% to 10.6% over the past few games. The Celtics still have an ORB% of 28.9% as a team, which is 11th in the NBA. However, their defensive rebounding has them sunk to 69%, which is 27th in the league. Sure, Tatum and the Celtics need to score more. However, rebounding remains their biggest woe. Robinson was acquired for this specific reason, but he hasn't been much help so far. Can Coach Mazzulla conjure up schemes to patch all of these problems after getting exposed by the Rockets? item.title: Winnacunnet field hockey leads Seacoast selections on NH all-state teams
item.description: Four Seacoast programs were well represented when the New Hampshire Field Hockey Coaches Association announced its Division I all-state selections on Monday, Nov. 2. Winnacunnet, Dover, Exeter and Portsmouth combined for four first-team selections, four second-team picks and 22 honorable mention recipients. Winnacunnet, which capped its season with a 3-2 loss to Pinkerton Academy in the Division I state championship game on Oct. 31, placed McKinley Fowler, Fiona McAfee and Sofia Donatelli on the first team. McAfee finished the season with 20 goals and 16 assists, Fowler had 17 goals and five assists, and Donatelli added 14 goals and 14 assists. "I am proud of these three," Winnacunnet head coach Heidi Hand said. "They led the scoring line for me and worked well as a team." Dover's Scarlett Gray was named to the first team, while Molly Angers earned second-team honors. Exeter's Amalia Gloss and Portsmouth's Izzy Getman were also named to the second team. The Seacoast schools were heavily represented among the honorable mention selections. Dover's Hannah Calhoun, Rylie Phillips, Kate Lavoie and Ella Deroy earned honorable mention. "This group is made up of an incredibly hard-working, dedicated, and talented group of young women who represent our program with pride," Dover coach Sarah Michaud said. "Each of them brings something special to our team, whether it’s their work ethic, commitment, leadership, or willingness to put the team first. We're so proud of everything they have accomplished and grateful for the impact they have made on our program. These girls are truly deserving of this recognition." Exeter had seven players earn honorable mention recognition, including Dylan Valade, Callan Myers, Maisie Meyers, Kelsey Hayward, Rowan Decew, Emma Amarosa and Jane Lyons. "I am incredibly proud of all of Exeter athletes named to all-state teams for their hard work, and dedication this season," Exeter head coach Deb Grott said. "Seeing their talent and leadership recognized is a testament to everything they have given the program." Winnacunnet's honorable mention selections were Mary Kouloheras, Julia Kouloheras, Kelly Curtin, Marley Eaton, Riley Gagalis, Zoe Tanida and Megan Kelly. item.title: Rutgers basketball 2026-27: Reasons to hope and mope, must-see games, prediction
item.description: These are unprecedented times for the Rutgers basketball program. Head coach Steve Pikiell is battling cancer, sparking a “Rutgers Tough” movement in the process. The Scarlet Knights finally caught up with the Joneses in terms of roster funding and hiring a general manager. Outside prognostications expect little of this team, but there were tantalizing preseason glimpses. What to make of all this? Here’s a look at how it might unfold for the Scarlet Knights as the 2026-27 season gets underway with a home game against New Haven on Nov. 6. 3 REASONS TO HOPE 1. A promising postman Rutgers’ glaring weakness last season was its post play, which was mostly nonexistent. Priority No. 1 was finding an impact center and 6-foot-10, 265-pound Virginia Tech transfer Christian Gurdak appears to be just that. In exhibitions against Villanova and St. John’s the sophomore averaged 19.5 points, 11.5 rebounds and 2.0 assists while shooting 50 percent from the field. He’s legit. 2. A solid returning core Six players returned – a high number in the free-agency era – and three of them are starters. Senior guard Tariq Francis was honorable mention All-Big Ten last winter, and he won’t have to carry the offensive load this season. Expect by leaps by senior forward Darren Buchanan and sophomore guard Lino Mark, both of whom played well in the preseason. Senior guard Jamichael Davis is a rare four-year Scarlet Knight. These guys know the system, the culture and the Big Ten. 3. The Big Dance expanded The move from 68 to 76 teams was mostly panned by the public, but it’s now highly likely that a 10-10 Big Ten record – something Rutgers has achieved four times under the current regime – punches a ticket. On paper there’s a fair amount of parity in the conference. Can this seemingly improved squad find four more league wins than last year? It doesn’t seem far-fetched. 3 REASONS TO MOPE 1. Big-man depth Beyond Gurdak, it’s all questions marks. Will Sydnor, a 6-8 transfer forward from Manhattan projected to have a big role, missed most of the offseason with a high ankle sprain. Freshman Mervedi Miteo and sophomore Gevonte Ware are blank canvasses. Backup center Dorin Buca missed both exhibition games. The Big Ten is a big man’s league. Gurdak can’t go it alone. 2. The defensive learning curve The onset of free agency turned a Rutgers strength – team defense – into a weakness as newcomers struggled to catch on to the concepts and the ethos that in the past was ingrained over a period of years. item.description: Scott Parker will once again be in the dugout at the London Stadium, after his Burnley side were beaten 3-2 there last November [Shutterstock] West Ham United have confirmed the appointment of former midfielder Scott Parker as their new head coach on a two-and-a-half-year contract. The 46-year-old replaces Nuno Espirito Santo, who was sacked on Tuesday after the club's disappointing start to the Championship season. Parker previously led Fulham, Bournemouth and Burnley to promotion from the Championship, but has been out of work since leaving the Clarets in April after their relegation from the Premier League. He will take charge of the team for the first time on Wednesday when West Ham travel to Cardiff City in the Championship. West Ham approach Parker after sacking boss Nuno Green backs 'proven' Parker for Hammers job Pragmatic Parker or a top flight contender? First-team coaches Steve Potts, Gerard Prenderville and Billy Lepine will assist Parker while his former team-mate Mark Noble will also work closely with him in his role as sporting director. The club will also make further announcements on the backroom team in the coming days and weeks. "It is a very proud moment for me to step into this role and return to a club that means so much to me and my family," Parker told the club website. "There was a warmth, a love, a feeling that I probably didn't have anywhere else. There was something which stood out constantly and that was the relationship that I built up with the fanbase here. That rapport and respect, that I felt instantly. "More than anything, this is an opportunity that I am very excited about. I feel privileged and honoured to be the guy that wants to lead us back to the Premier League and be the head coach of this football club at this moment in time. "My energy levels, my enthusiasm, my desire, my passion - it's absolutely running through and that's the feeling I had as soon as there was a conversation that this was possible. That's exactly why I'm here and why I want to be here." item.title: Real Madrid closing in on deal for Man United prodigy JJ Gabriel ahead of Bayern, PSG and Barcelona
item.description: Real Madrid closing in on deal for Man United prodigy JJ Gabriel ahead of Bayern, PSG and Barcelona Bayern Munich have reportedly been dealt a setback in their pursuit of highly rated 16-year-old Manchester United prodigy JJ Gabriel. According to Sky Germany, Real Madrid have reached a verbal agreement in principle with the youngster and are now looking to finalise the transfer. However, nothing has been signed yet, with Bayern Munich, Paris Saint-Germain and Barcelona all still hoping for a late change of heart. Bayern have remained in contact with the player's representatives throughout the process, but as things stand, they are considered outsiders in the race to sign him. One reason for this is the overall financial package Real Madrid are able to offer, which includes a significant salary as well as a substantial signing-on bonus and agent fees.

item.title: Former inmate-turned-Tigers star Ron LeFlore's story told in new book
item.description: Going from a Michigan prison straight to professional baseball, former Detroit Tigers player Ron LeFlore , 78, inspired a TV movie, a best-selling memoir and a huge fandom among Tigers fans during his MLB tenure in Detroit. But though one of Detroit's most popular and productive players of the 1970s (his 14.3 Baseball Reference WAR from 1970-79 lands him second in the decade among Tigers position players), he's not often mentioned as a franchise legend. Bay Area author Adam Henig explores the Detroit native in his 2026 book, " Baseball's Outcast: The Story of Ron LeFlore ," a biography of one of the most talented Tigers players of all time. Henig lays out LeFlore's life from an impoverished childhood on Detroit's east side, to a prison stint, to a dramatic development as an MLB star, with LeFlore's playing career shortened by drugs and conflicts with managers and team executives. Henig's book also picks up where LeFlore's memoir left off, mapping out the star's life after baseball and his legacy in Tigers history. In his discussions with LeFlore's family, former teammates and former Free Press writers, Henig also reveals several details about LeFlore's career in baseball and what eventually led to the game turning away from him. The Free Press spoke to Henig about his writing process and thoughts about LeFlore, with the following interview edited for length and clarity. Author Adam Henig on Ron LeFlore's life LeFlore's early life When did you first hear about Ron LeFlore and what inspired you to write the book? "It really begins when I was about 8 or 9 years old. I wasn't much of a reader growing up as a child, and the only thing I would read were books about baseball. And my mom, who was a school teacher, had noticed this book about Ron LeFlore. It was a children's version of his memoir that had come out some about 45 years ago, called "From Prison to the Major Leagues." And she's like, "I think you might like this," and I did. "When I was trying to figure out what I was going to write about after publishing my third book back in 2020, I was curious what had happened to Ron. He had led a fascinating life, being someone who was incarcerated and then being directly recruited out of prison by a Major League Baseball organization. [It's] not only unusual, it would never happen today." A lot of the early parts of the book were about his family and, specifically, his older brother Harry. How much do you think Harry's death impacted Ron's trajectory? "Ron was, I believe, 10 years old when his oldest brother died. And he wasn't just a brother, he was a role model. item.title: H.C. Hurricane named to North Carolina vs. South Carolina Shrine Bowl Game
item.description: Hampton County High School Hurricane football standout Ja'Shon Williams has named to the roster of the South Carolina team for the 2026 North Carolina vs. South Carolina Shrine Bowl Game on Dec. 19 in Spartanburg. This is a classic all-star football game featuring the top high school players from the Palmetto State, pitted against the top players from North Carolina's high schools. “I’m very grateful for this opportunity to represent my family, team, and county in this historic all-star game," said Williams. "My teammates have been a major part in me having this opportunity by always encouraging me to work hard even after I’m exhausted. This so no doubt in my mind that the hard work my team and I have put in since the spring will be showcased.” Williams will be the first athlete selected for this honor from the newly consolidated Hampton County Hurricane program. The school was formerly known as Wade Hampton High School. "Hampton County High School had a player named to the team in 2021, but the game wasn't played due to Covid, so Ja'Shon will be our first Hurricane to play in the Shrine Bowl Game," said Hurricanes Head Coach Robert Hanna. "Way to go Ja'Shon!" "We are so proud of Ja'Shon for being named to this team," Coach Hanna added. "This is a big honor for him and the HCHS Football program as being chosen as one of the top players in the state. There have not been many from Hampton County make this game in roughly the past five, and I'm excited for him to experience this opportunity of playing in a game with some of the best players in the country." item.title: Three Bargain Starting Pitching Targets for San Diego
item.description: Oct 7, 2026; Cumberland, Georgia, USA; Atlanta Braves pitcher Tyler Mahle (54) pitches during the second inning against the Los Angeles Dodgers in game four of the NLDS for the 2026 MLB Playoffs at Truist Park. Mandatory Credit: Brett Da… | Source: Lastwordonsports.com - Augustus Oswald, Site Editor It’s no secret that the San Diego Padres are in desperate need of starting pitching. The Friars declined Nick Pivetta’s $14 million club option , leaving only Randy Vásquez as a viable starting rotation piece. JP Sears continues to be unproven, and Joe Musgrove likely won’t begin the season in the starting rotation. With Michael King departing in free agency , the Padres need to sign some starting pitchers. Here are three bargain pitchers that San Diego can target this offseason. 3 Bargain Starting Pitching Targets for San Diego RHP Tyler Mahle In 27 starts (149.0 IP) this season, Tyler Mahle posted a 3.99 ERA, 1.23 WHIP, and a .248 opponent batting average. The journeyman pitcher struggled with injuries in the last few years, starting just 24 games from 2023-25. Prior to that, he had been solid in six big-league seasons. He was signed to a one-year, $10 million deal with the San Francisco Giants ahead of the 2026 season to modest results (5.13 ERA, 94 2/3 IP). Sep 18, 2026; Houston, Texas, USA; Atlanta Braves starting pitcher Tyler Mahle (54) delivers a pitch during the second inning against the Houston Astros at Daikin Park. Mandatory Credit: Troy Taormina-Imagn Images After that, San Francisco traded Mahle to the Atlanta Braves, where he flourished. In 54 1/3 innings of work, Mahle pitched to a 1.99 ERA, 0.96 WHIP, and .216 opponent batting average. In the entirety of his time with San Francisco (18 games), Mahle accumulated -0.1 Wins Above Replacement (WAR). He accumulated 1.8 WAR with Atlanta in half of the time he was with the Giants (nine games). Mahle is projected to receive a three-year, $48 million contract at $16 million average annual value (AAV). His injury history makes it a worrisome deal for San Diego, but he could still add value in the back end of the rotation. Alternatively, Mahle could also be given a short-term, higher-AAV deal. A contract with the Friars seems unlikely if a bidding war ensues, but San Diego could scoop him up on an affordable, short-term deal. LHP Kris Bubic Kris Bubic posted incredible numbers in 2025, pitching to a 2.55 ERA over 116 1/3 innings. His season ended early due to a rotator cuff injury, limiting him to 20 starts. The left-hander dealt with multiple arm injuries in 2026, as well as a stop-and-start recovery. He was solid while on the field, making 14 appearances and posting a 3.76 ERA between the Kansas City Royals and Los Angeles Dodgers . item.description: FBL-EUR-C1-VILLARREAL-PSG - AFP Paris Saint-Germain midfielder Fabian Ruiz paid an emotional tribute to late CD Tenerife forward Jesus de Miguel after netting twice in Tuesday's emphatic 6-0 Champions League triumph away at Villarreal. The Spain international held up nine fingers and pointed to the sky after scoring his first goal at the Estadio de la Ceramica. Spanish playmaker honours fallen compatriot Ruiz used his 17th-minute strike on Matchday 4 to honour Miguel by forming the striker's number nine shirt with his hands before looking towards the heavens. item.title: Quentin Koch chose Xavier for its tradition. Now he's chasing an Open title against his old team
item.description: Quentin Koch of Xavier edges out Gabriel White of E.O. Smith in the Boys Class MM division during the CIAC Boys Cross Country Championships held Saturday, October 31, 2026 at Wickham Park in Manchester. (Jim Shannon/Hearst Connecticut Media) Quentin Koch has long known about the Xavier boys cross country program. He followed it for years, then decided that was where he wanted to be. Koch transferred from Greenwich to Xavier after two seasons of cross country with the Cardinals. On Saturday, Koch was Xavier's top runner at the Class MM championships at Wickham Park in Manchester. He finished second in 15:50.9 and helped the Falcons score 31 points to win the MM team title by a wide margin. It was Xavier's eighth straight class title. The Falcons have won the last two MM crowns after taking six straight in Class L. "The training, it's tight and everyone holds each other accountable. It's not a hostile environment, but it's a hard-working environment, and it only elevates the guys around it," said Koch, a junior. "It's all love, and everybody's best friends on the team. That makes it so much easier. We're always out there in the mornings, working hard, getting the runs in." Koch improved by nearly 46 seconds on his best time at Greenwich. The lure for Koch when it came to Xavier was the program. "Just knowing the guys, I really wanted to be a part of it. It's so special. Every day in practice, I look forward to it," Koch said. "That's honestly probably the biggest change. I wanted to elevate myself and try to take myself as high as I can, and I think it's definitely showing." Koch has fit right in with his new team . In an ironic twist, the State Open on Thursday could set up a showdown between Koch's new team and his old one. Greenwich won the Class LL title in dominating fashion, scoring 24 points and finishing well ahead of second-place Southington (113). Like Xavier, Greenwich got a terrific performance from its top five scorers. The Cardinals, led by individual champion James Hayes (16:19.3) and runner-up Vihaan Kamath (16:23.6), finished first, second, fourth (William Monaco, 16:30.4), eighth (Oliver Eaton, 16:36.5) and ninth (Aiden Towle, 16:44.4). "(Xavier hasn't) won one (State Open) in a few years (2018), so we definitely want to bring some hardware back," Koch said. "This is the best the team has looked in a while honestly. I've been following the program, and it's historic. You go to the CIAC (online), and you know Xavier." Koch believes the Falcons need to keep doing what they're doing to win an Open championship. "You can't let the emotions get too high. Just staying level and I think we do it. It's ours to lose," Koch said. Sign up for the Connecticut Briefing from CT Insider. The Australian scored within six minutes as Chelsea went on to win 2-0 and has made a key impact for the Blues on several occasions this season. "I made the final decision and someone in my technical staff said: 'But we need to score, and you are bringing on a defensive player?'" said Bompastor. "We laughed after the game because I said: 'Right now, she's scoring a lot of goals, so I don't know if she's a more defensive or attacking player!' "It worked so it's good. Carpenter's 'licence to go forward' Unbeaten Chelsea are top of the Women's Super League table, having only dropped points in their opening weekend draw with Aston Villa. Carpenter has started all but one of their WSL matches and has netted four goals from a full-back or wing-back position. item.title: Stephen A. Smith makes Lamar Jackson prediction after injury as Ravens future remains uncertain
item.description: Photo by Rich von Biberstein/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Stephen A. Smith does not believe Lamar Jackson has played his final game for the Baltimore Ravens despite the quarterback facing a potentially season-ending thumb injury. Jackson is set to undergo surgery after leaving the Ravens’ 36-10 defeat to the Buffalo Bills with an injury to his right thumb. Head coach Jesse Minter confirmed the procedure could rule him out for the remainder of the campaign. The setback has also raised fresh questions about Jackson’s long-term future in Baltimore, with the two-time MVP entering the final year of his contract in 2027. Stephen A. Smith backs Lamar Jackson to remain with the Baltimore Ravens Speaking about Jackson’s future, Smith made it clear that he expects the quarterback to return to Baltimore rather than move elsewhere. “I do not (think he’s played his final game for the Ravens),” Smith said. He then explained why the Ravens would find it difficult to move on from their franchise quarterback, particularly given the difference he makes when available. “When Lamar Jackson is healthy and he’s on the football field, he is electrifying. You saw his QBR, which was top two in the league in the games that he played this year, you saw his passer rating, you saw his yards that he accumulated, and the man is electrifying. And without him, they don’t win games. He’s just that special. He’s that much of a difference maker.” Smith also described Baltimore as a championship contender whenever Jackson is fit, while acknowledging that his recent injury record has become a major concern. The financial situation is another complication. Jackson’s current contract runs through the 2027 season, but his $84.34 million salary cap figure for next year is considered difficult to manage given Baltimore’s position. The Ravens are reportedly $45.94 million over the 2027 cap, while Jackson has no-trade and no-franchise-tag clauses that give him significant control over his future. ESPN insider Dan Graziano has suggested Baltimore could consider a trade if another extension cannot be agreed, particularly with Jackson approaching the final year of his deal. However, Smith believes the Ravens should be reluctant to take that risk. Jackson remains one of the NFL’s most influential quarterbacks when healthy, and Baltimore’s struggles without him have only reinforced his importance. With surgery now ahead of him, Jackson’s immediate priority will be recovering from the thumb injury. His next contract decision could prove just as important for the Ravens.
